claims.text: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said on Wednesday that a joint statement with Oman regarding a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz is in the final review and drafting stage.
Donald Trump stated late Tuesday that an agreement regarding the Strait of Hormuz is imminent.
Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz was freely open to all maritime traffic.
US officials have repeatedly insisted that they would never accept an agreement permitting Iran to control access to the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated, 'The factors making the Strait of Hormuz insecure still exist on the part of the United States, particularly the naval blockade and other aggressive and threatening actions against Iran and its interests.'
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that the proposed new shipping route would be temporary and remain open for two to four months.
Tehran has largely blocked the Strait of Hormuz since the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran in late February.
Approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas typically passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have maintained a blockade on Saudi Arabian Red Sea ports since July 20.
Reuters reported that the draft agreement under discussion would place inbound commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz under Iranian control.
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that parts of the planned shipping route would cross Iranian territorial waters while other sections would pass through Omani waters.
US Central Command stated on Wednesday that it had redirected 48 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two as part of its naval blockade.
Former public health official Abdul El-Sayed won the Michigan Democratic primary election for the US Senate.
Groups linked to AIPAC spent $30 million on negative advertisements targeting Abdul El-Sayed during his primary campaign.
Donald Trump stated during a Nevada campaign rally that Abdul El-Sayed 'doesn't love Israel. He doesn't love Jewish people. He hates them.'
Abdul El-Sayed defeated Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary election for the US Senate in Michigan.
State Representative Donavan McKinney defeated two-term Congressman Shri Thanedar in Michigan's 13th Congressional District Democratic primary with 51.9 percent of the vote to 48.1 percent.
Donavan McKinney was endorsed by Senator Bernie Sanders, Representative Rashida Tlaib, Justice Democrats, and Leaders We Deserve.
Outside political groups supported Haley Stevens over Abdul El-Sayed by a nine-to-one financial margin.
Abdul El-Sayed will face former Republican congressman Mike Rogers in the general election for the US Senate in Michigan.
In Missouri's Democratic congressional primary, Wesley Bell defeated incumbent representative Cori Bush.
More than 40 people were injured across Kyiv and surrounding areas during Russian missile and drone strikes.
Russia launched 115 drones and 24 ballistic missiles in an overnight attack against targets across Ukraine.
At least 17 people were killed following an overnight Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv and its surrounding region.
Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 98 of 115 Russian drones overnight but failed to shoot down any ballistic missiles.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that air defense interceptor supplies delivered to Ukraine during the first half of 2026 fell to one-third of the levels supplied in 2025.
Seven sites were struck in Kyiv during Wednesday's attack, including a brewing company, construction material warehouses, and a railway station.
The Kyiv military administration stated that the Russian attack caused an ammonia leak that emergency crews were dispatched to manage.
Donetsk region governor Vadym Filashkin ordered hundreds of families with children to evacuate the city of Kramatorsk due to escalating Russian strikes.
An Israeli airstrike hit the roof of a cemetery prayer hall in Tibnin, Lebanon, killing one person and injuring 12 others.
The Israeli military issued an evacuation order for residents of Mansouri, Lebanon, marking its first evacuation directive in over a month.
The UN humanitarian office reported that over 820,000 displaced persons in Lebanon returned home, while approximately 360,000 remain displaced.
Two Israeli soldiers were killed and another was critically injured when an explosive device detonated inside a booby-trapped building in Majdal Selem.
Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli attacks have killed at least 4,333 people and wounded 12,250 others in Lebanon since March 2.
Israeli forces detonated 700 tons of explosives in a demolition operation around Beaufort Castle outside Nabatieh.
At least 40 Israelis, including 38 soldiers, have been killed by Hezbollah since March 2.
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani contacted Iran's foreign minister to request that Tehran halt Hezbollah's military operations.
Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem stated that direct negotiations with Israel would bring 'nothing but shame, humiliation' and successive concessions for Lebanon.
An explosive-laden drone was discovered by an employee in the cargo operations area near the south runway at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt stated regarding the drone discovery, 'We are dealing here with a competition that may also include foreign powers... who quite obviously want to contribute to considerable uncertainty in Germany.'
A DHL cargo plane aborted landing at Leipzig and subsequently collided mid-air with an unidentified object, sustaining minor damage before landing in Hanover.
Ukraine's ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev stated to Welt TV regarding the drone incident, 'Who else could it be but Russia?'
Leipzig/Halle Airport serves as a maintenance base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines and a transit hub for German military and NATO goods.
German police removed the detonator from the drone discovered at Leipzig airport and subsequently executed a controlled explosion.
German police found up to 800 grams of plastic explosive attached to the drone discovered at Leipzig airport.
German state prosecutors, including units focused on terrorism and extremism, took over the investigation into the Leipzig airport drone incident.
Deposed Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced during a virtual press conference in New Delhi that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December.
Bangladesh's foreign ministry issued a statement expressing outrage that India permitted Sheikh Hasina to hold a live press interaction in New Delhi.
A special tribunal in Dhaka sentenced Sheikh Hasina to death in absentia in 2025 for alleged crimes against humanity.
According to the United Nations, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the 2024 youth-led uprising in Bangladesh.
Sheikh Hasina's son, Sajeeb Wazed, participated in the New Delhi press conference via video link from Washington, D.C.
Following elections in February, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party assumed power with Tarique Rahman becoming prime minister.
Sheikh Hasina demanded that Bangladesh lift the ban on the Awami League party and release political prisoners.
Cockroach Janta Party chief spokesperson Saurav Das filed a police complaint alleging that 15 to 20 media persons and YouTubers filmed inside his home without consent.
Activist Sonam Wangchuk completed a 26-day hunger strike in Delhi during June and July demanding examination and education reforms.
Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following sustained youth-led protests over leaked examination papers.
Graduate unemployment in India has remained between 35 percent and 40 percent over the past 25 years.
Meta temporarily removed a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during student protests before restoring it and citing an automated moderation error.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke announced in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar that the outfit will operate as a pressure group rather than contesting elections.
Cockroach Janta Party members announced plans to travel to Ranchi to back candidates protesting alleged exam irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant observed during a Supreme Court hearing, 'The biggest powerful source is listening, listening to what they are saying and why they are agitating.'
Meta's Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan stated, 'I apologised to the minister on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post.'
Parliamentary Standing Committee chairman Nishikant Dubey issued a three-day deadline for Mark Zuckerberg to tender an apology over the temporary removal of PM Modi's video.
Meta representatives admitted to Indian officials that paid promotion on its platforms resulted in illegal content being amplified.
Indian IT ministry officials informed Meta executives that algorithmic content curation disqualifies the company from safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act.
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and IT demanded that Google India lose its safe harbour protection following cyberfraud complaints linked to Play Store apps.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video post addressing students about paper leaks was temporarily restricted on Facebook on July 23.
Meta attributed the restriction of PM Modi's Facebook post to a technical glitch within its automated AI content filtering system.
A BBC Eye investigation identified approximately 30 advertisements on Instagram promoting child sexual abuse material.
